newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Some rolling out of January seen.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Some rolling out of January seen.

text.p: Index options investors were seen rolling positions out of the January series, which expires in a week and a half, traders said Tuesday.
The action was particularly noteworthy in S&P 500 index .SPX options at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
"There was a lot of unwinding at the beginning of the day, people trying to get out of positions," one index options trader at the CME said. "People were trying to buy March and sell January."
He said the market's weakness contributed to the desire to sell January positions ahead of their expiration January 18.
"The market seems a bit heavy," the trader said. "People are looking to keep bids on the downside a little more firm than they would normally."
By 1110 CST/1710 GMT, the underlying SPX cash index was down about 3.50 points at 744, about two points off its session low.

The lead March S&P 500 futures contract was down 1.10 at 749.60, having traded between 746.60 and 751.70. Traders pegged fair value at 5.08 points, with arbitrage sell programs at a premium of 4.50 points and arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 6.20 points.
Traders noted light sell programs in early activity.
The trader at the CME said the January 700 puts and March 715 puts were among the most active as an investor did a put calendar spread with those several hundred times.
Index options traders at the Chicago Board Options Exchange said action there was relatively quiet, with the focus remaining on the put side.
"There's nothing special going on," one said, adding that people were not yet talking about key economic data due on Thursday and Friday.
December U.S. producer price data are due Thursday, followed by the key December U.S. employment report Friday.
Some of the biggest trades were seen in deep out-of-the-money March puts on the SPX, where the March 680 put traded more than 6,000 contracts and the March 700 put traded nearly 5,000.
Six thousand of the March 680 puts crossed as a spread and most of the March 700 put volume was in small blocks.
In the S&P 100 index .OEX, where the bulk of index options trading takes place, activity continued to be skewed toward puts, led by the January 700 and 725s.
The OEX January 700 put, which had open interest of 21,089 through Monday, when 777 new contracts were added, traded about 4,300 contracts.
The January 725 put traded about 4,120. Its open interest was 13,601 and included an addition of 3,265 contracts Monday.
The cash OEX index was off 1.31 at 730.31 after falling to an intraday low of 726.61.
